title: Context Window Optimization
summary: Allocate finite model context to the evidence and state that matter, preserving constraints and enough capacity for a complete response.
overview: Context window optimization selects, compresses, and orders information within a model’s input and output limits. A large supported window does not imply that every included token contributes equally to answer quality. Long histories can add irrelevant detail, conflicting instructions, and substantial prefill cost.

The useful abstraction is a context budget with protected and optional segments. System constraints, current task facts, and indispensable evidence receive explicit allocation; old dialogue and redundant retrieval receive selective retention or summarization. Summaries are derived artifacts and should retain provenance, unresolved decisions, and links to recover original detail.

production.poc: A prototype measures token use and answer quality as conversation length grows.
production.production: Production reserves output capacity, compacts history at defined thresholds, and tests whether critical facts survive compaction.
production.scale: Enterprise scale tracks budget use by task, supports versioned summaries, and evaluates long-context alternatives against retrieval and selective reconstruction.

components.name: Token estimator
components.role: Counts the actual request format using the selected model’s tokenizer or supported estimate.

components.name: Segment allocator
components.role: Reserves mandatory policy, current task, evidence, and output capacity.

components.name: History compactor
components.role: Produces bounded summaries with source references and unresolved commitments.

components.name: Evidence selector
components.role: Removes duplication and chooses passages supporting the requested answer.

components.name: Context evaluator
components.role: Tests fact retention, contradiction handling, and response completeness.

flow.title: Inventory context
flow.description: Classify candidate segments by trust, freshness, relevance, and required retention.

flow.title: Reserve fixed capacity
flow.description: Allocate mandatory instructions and an adequate output budget before optional text.

flow.title: Select evidence
flow.description: Keep passages covering distinct answer requirements rather than merely the highest similarity scores.

flow.title: Compact history
flow.description: Summarize older dialogue while preserving decisions, identifiers, and unresolved obligations.

flow.title: Validate the final request
flow.description: Count serialized tokens and confirm protected facts and constraints remain present.

flow.title: Recover detail when needed
flow.description: Retrieve original records if a later task requires information omitted by compaction.

useCase.title: Maintaining a long design-review conversation
useCase.situation: A design assistant follows weeks of decisions about an industrial control upgrade.
useCase.problem: Old alternatives and repeated documents crowd out current constraints and requested analysis.
useCase.requirement: Preserve approved decisions and unresolved questions without resending every turn.
useCase.architecture: A decision ledger and versioned conversation summary feed a context allocator with targeted source retrieval.
runtime: The current task asks about a previously deferred interface decision.
The allocator retrieves the original decision record and adds only the relevant discussion around it.
useCase.failure: If the summary conflicts with the authoritative decision ledger, the ledger wins and the summary is rebuilt.
useCase.impact: Measure retained-constraint accuracy, input tokens, and complete-answer rate; shrinking the prompt is useful only if required reasoning evidence survives.

tradeoffs.cost: Can lose details or distort commitments.
Increase latency and do not guarantee effective use.

failures.detection: Generated summary disagrees with recorded approval.
failures.recovery: Use authoritative decision fields and validate summary claims.

failures.detection: Responses end before required sections complete.
failures.recovery: Reserve output capacity and reduce optional input.

mistakes.mistake: Truncating from the oldest token blindly
mistakes.fix: Preserve commitments and durable identifiers explicitly.

mistakes.mistake: Treating summary text as ground truth
mistakes.fix: Retain source links and recover originals.
Evaluate task quality and constraint retention.

whenToUse: Use for long conversations and large retrieved contexts.
Use when prefill cost dominates response time.
Use when repeated evidence crowds out current task facts.
whenNotToUse: Avoid compression when exact wording is essential and fits comfortably.
Do not remove safety or authorization constraints to save tokens.
checklist: Version summaries and their source ranges.
Support retrieval of omitted original details.
